world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Drabbe, Peter. 1954. Talen en dialecten van zuid-west Nieuw-Guinea (Micro-Bibliotheca Anthropos 11) — Yei grammar sketch; no online copy found. Also Nevermann 1942 Die Je-Nan

sources.citation: WALS Online, language 'Yei' (wals code yei): 16 datapoints, all coded from Boelaars 1950.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only word-order/negation/tense-affix features; no stress (Goedemans & van der Hulst) datapoints for Yei.

sources.citation: Evans, Nicholas. 2021. The phonetics of Papuan languages in Southern New Guinea: an overview. In: Phonetic fieldwork in Southern New Guinea (LD&C Special Publication 24), 1-?.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Areal remark only (p. 7): SNG phonologies share 'absences (e.g., no tone, no pitch accent or distinctive stress except for Urama..)' - refers to the languages in that volume (Yelmek, Ngkolmpu, Nmbo, Idi, Bitur, Urama, Nen, Ende); Yei is not treated.

sources.citation: Carroll, Matthew J. 2020. The morphology of Yam languages. Oxford Research Encyclopedia of Linguistics. doi:10.1093/acrefore/9780199384655.013.677 (ANU open copy, hdl 1885/220610).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Yei data from the author's own fieldwork (Po village, July 2019); case, pronouns, verb prefixes/suffixes. States 'The state of research on the Yei language/s is only just beginning'. Silent on stress.

sources.citation: Evans, Nicholas. 2012. Even more diverse than we had thought: the multiplicity of Trans-Fly languages. In Evans & Klamer (eds), Melanesian Languages on the Edge of Asia (LD&C Special Publication 5), 109-149.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Yei mentioned only for classification (third branch of Yam) and language shift; nothing on Yei phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Sohn, Myo-Sook, Randy Lebold & Ronald Kriens. 2009. Report on the Merauke Subdistrict Survey, Papua, Indonesia. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2009-018. 46 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No prose on stress. Appendix V gives a 239-item IPA wordlist with a 'Yei: Poo' column carrying primary/secondary stress marks (e.g. 'kilpel' head with initial stress mark, m@'natSEr woman with second-syllable mark) - raw data only.

sources.citation: Sohn, Myo-Sook. 2006. Report on the Muting District Survey [Papua, Indonesia]. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2006-006. 10+ pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Section 5.4 'The Yei Language': lexicostatistics only (Tanas vs Poo 51% similarity, possibly two languages); wordlists not printed; silent on stress.

sources.citation: van Baal, Jan. 1982. Jan Verschueren's Description of Yei-nan Culture, extracted from the posthumous papers. Verhandelingen KITLV 99. The Hague: Nijhoff. (OAPEN open access)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ethnography. Preface pp. XII-XIII discusses only orthographic choices (e = schwa or e/E, a vs long a marked with acute, j, y, v/w) and notes that the linguistic record is Geurtjens' 450-item list plus 'Drabbe's grammatical outline of the Yei language (10 pages)' in MBA 11 and Boelaars 1950. Silent on stress.

sources.citation: Boelaars, J. H. M. C. 1950. The Linguistic Position of South-Western New Guinea. Leiden: E. J. Brill (Utrecht dissertation). Chapter VIII 'Jei-language', pp. 49-54 (from P. Drabbe's field notes). Delpher urn MMKB35:171580000.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, HathiTrust search-only; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number 2234.104.2; Widener Library (offsite storage), call number KF 19825)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number 2234.104.2; Widener Library (offsite storage), call number KF 19825
sources.note: No rule. Preface (pp. xx-xxi, seq 20-22): 'Drabbe has checked all the details of Part I and indicated the stress marks. This notation is not meant to be the last word in connection with pitch, accent etc.. a bold lettertype indicates stress. Although we do not discuss the phonological items of these languages..'. So stress is only marked typographically (bold vowel) on individual cited Jei forms (page images of pp. 49-54 saved); the Jei chapter itself is nouns/pronouns/numerals/verbs/linking-elements only.

sources.citation: Nevermann, Hans. 1942. Die Je-Nan. Baessler-Archiv 24: 87-221. (whole-volume scanned plaintext from Staatliche Museen zu Berlin digi-hub, record PI 1500894752795)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Read the section 'SPRACHE' (print pp. 203-211): dialect differences, frequent reduction of full vowels to a pepet-like e, s > dz/tz, reduplication, pronouns, possessives, verb paradigms, comparative word list. Nothing on Betonung/Akzent; silent on stress.

sources.citation: Drabbe, Peter. 1954. Talen en dialecten van Zuid-West Nieuw-Guinea (Deel: Aantekeningen over drie talen tussen Mbian en Fly: Moraori, Jei en Kanum). Micro-Bibliotheca Anthropos 11. Posieux/Fribourg: Institut Anthropos. 257 pp. (microfilm)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: held in print at Harvard (Tozzer Library, call number Microfilm L.SOC.12.70.6.13 (11)); ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.harvard_location: Tozzer Library, call number Microfilm L.SOC.12.70.6.13 (11)
sources.note: The only primary grammatical sketch of Yei (c. 10 pp.); Boelaars 1950 states Drabbe 'indicated the stress marks' for these data, and Drabbe's other south-coast sketches carry a 'klemtoon' paragraph, so this is the single most likely place for an explicit stress statement.

sources.citation: Evans, Nicholas & Sebastian Fedden (eds.). (forthcoming/2025). The Oxford Guide to the Papuan Languages. Oxford: OUP - Yam-family chapter(s) (Carroll, Doehler, Evans, Kashima, Siegel).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Expected to contain an up-to-date Yam phonology overview including Yei prosody, drawing on Carroll's 2019-2021 fieldwork.

sources.citation: Carroll, Matthew J. 2019-2021. Pan-dialectal documentation of the Yei language. ELAR deposit yei-carroll-0563 (ELDP IPF0283), hdl 2196/00-0000-0000-0012-D793-C; plus any sketch grammar / phonology write-up arising from it (none published as of the ANU repository listing).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: no other copy located; the open copy could not be downloaded when a reader tried
sources.note: The only modern in-depth documentation of Yei (Po, Torai, Bupul, Tanas, Kwel dialects); a phonology sketch by Carroll, if/when written, would supersede everything above. Worth asking the depositor directly.

sources.citation: Evans, Nicholas, I Wayan Arka, Matthew Carroll, Yun Jung Choi, Christian Doehler, Volker Gast, Eri Kashima, Emil Mittag, Bruno Olsson, Kyla Quinn, Dineke Schokkin, Philip Tama, Charlotte van Tongeren & Jeff Siegel. 2018. The languages of Southern New Guinea. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide, 641-774. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.

sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Modern family-level survey with a Yam section (phoneme inventories, typological profile) written with Yei fieldworkers (Mittag, Carroll) as co-authors; may state the Yam/Yei prosodic type (no tone; stress placement).

sources.citation: Geurtjens, Hendrik. 1933. Woordenlijsten der talen die het Marindineesche taalgebied begrenzen. In Marindineesch-Nederlandsch Woordenboek (Verhandelingen Bataviaasch Genootschap 71:5), 397-429. Bandoeng: Nix.
